correctness.rationale: The doubled-angle projector formula converts each layer's tightness to zero sum of five unit phasors, and converts a phasor real inner product x to squared overlap (1+x)/2. The proposed triplet and pair have real sums s and -s, with s^2=3/2; cycling the triplet preserves tightness. Reconstructing the three accumulated overlaps gives (s^2-3)/2 within the triplet, -s^2/2 across the blocks, and 3(s^2/2-1) in the fixed pair. All are -3/4, so the squared overlaps average 3/8 for all ten pairs. The two pentagonal frequency rows have zero sum; the real part of the sum over the four nontrivial fifth roots yields the required two-frequency sum -1/2 at every nonzero offset. Stacking the size-2 and size-3 constructions generates every R>=2 while preserving the weighted average and all layer identities. Tightness makes the one-layer constant 3/8, so the doubled-angle Gram matrix would have eigenvalue 5/4 four times and rank four in a plane, impossible.
residual_risks: This is existence with aligned column indices and repeated layers allowed; it does not classify realizations or assert higher-dimensional existence.
